prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System: decision support for dry, steep, windy wildland-urban interface terrain. Baseline: segmentation, time sync, health checks, audit logging. Caldera Incident Command Portal (alias Emberhall): primary UI/common operating picture with role-based symbology; opens triage case above threshold, records reasons; may set Airspace Restricted State; marks failed bridge route impaired; holds jurisdictional constraints before Drone Pilot Operator briefing; shows crew acks; produces Crew Staging Pin (effective time, location accuracy, incident ID); promotes accepted fire location to operational map for aviation review; input conflicts need review before promotion. Map products record source/processing time, model version, analyst acceptance, supersession. North Lookout Camera Mast: sends Thermal Spot Snippet, smoke bearing. South Lookout Camera Mast: sends bearing track; produces Camera Cleaning Log. Horizon Ridge Drone Dock (alias Kestrel): keeps aircraft charged/ready; produces Battery Swap Ticket; must report launch readiness, aircraft health, recovery availability before recon release. Drone Tasking Service: tasks Kestrel; makes missions (launch windows, image requirements, altitude limits, abort criteria); not flight-release authority; no launch conflicting with aviation lane. Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine (alias Lantern): advisory scores, provenance, perimeter; not final fireline until confidence, sensor age, positional error shown; compares recon, camera, weather projections. Fire behavior model: spread probability bands. Smoke Classifier Module: outputs to Lantern; produces Ridge Shadow Mask; never sole basis for aircraft commitment. MesoWest Weather Fusion Node (alias Brindle): publishes Wind Shift Bulletin, time-indexed weather updates. VHF Radio Gateway Repeater (alias Badger): fallback relay of approved aviation instructions. Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console (alias Marigold): tanker availability, ETA, turnaround, priority; must block release if approvals, airspace status, or readiness incomplete; produces Runway Release Note. East/West Retardant Loading Pumps: report equipment state, flow readiness, out-of-service; East sends Retardant Batch Slip to Tanker Base Manager. Loading status is informational, not approval. Crewline Mobile Tablet: Helitack Crew Leader acks. Actors: County Emergency Liaison (sends Drone Corridor Permit). Duty Detection Officer (alias Orion). Air Attack Supervisor (alias Redtail): reviews location, confidence history, airspace before authorizing; uses Wind Shift Bulletin. Tanker Base Manager: resolves discrepancies before release. Drone Pilot

New part:
S146: The Crewline Mobile Tablet shows approved suppression objectives, aircraft caution areas, and current assignment notes for crews operating near the incident.
S147: The Helitack Crew Leader acknowledges nearby aircraft activity before personnel are moved into a drop zone or a reconnaissance overflight area.
S148: The Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console sends the Suppression Drop Receipt after a completed drop has been recorded and checked for required timing fields.
S149: During extended attack, the Caldera Incident Command Portal preserves each aviation decision with the approving supervisor, operational period, and reason for change.
S150: The County Emergency Liaison can view approved aviation status and public safety implications without gaining authority to alter dispatch or suppression records.
S151: If reconnaissance, loading status, or weather guidance conflicts with an active plan, the system holds the affected recommendation for Air Attack Supervisor review before further action.
S152: This section describes how helitack and ground crews receive assignments, staging information, hazards, and updated intelligence from the support system during active wildfire operations.
S153: When a held recommendation is cleared, the Air Attack Supervisor selects the operational intent in the Caldera Incident Command Portal.
S154: The Caldera Incident Command Portal records each assignment package with an objective, time validity, confirmation status, and required acknowledgments.
S155: The Crewline Mobile Tablet displays the current division assignment, route guidance, rally location, and assigned communications channel for the logged-in crew.
S156: The Helitack Crew Leader receives the same operational package with aviation constraints and landing zone notes after Air Attack Supervisor approval.
S157: Ground crew assignments are formatted for field execution and avoid analytic scores that are not needed for tactical movement.
S158: Staging information is maintained as georeferenced areas and route descriptions so that crews can confirm location without relying on informal landmarks.
S159: The Crewline Mobile Tablet caches the latest accepted staging information and marks any expired package as unavailable for execution.
S160: If the Confirmed Ignition State changes the perimeter or priority area, the Caldera Incident Command Portal marks affected crew assignments for review before release.
S161: The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine updates hazard summaries when fire spread estimates, access constraints, or field observations change.
S162: The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine applies the Ridge Shadow Mask when estimating crew-visible fire edge confidence in steep terrain.
S163: The Smoke Classifier Module uses the Camera Cleaning Log to suppress confidence changes caused by lens contamination and service timing.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
